rulings.question: CWO-1 versus the letter-named acrostic key
rulings.decision: NARROW CWO-1, recorded as B3-1 dated 2026-09-07 - not a rewrite. P02-006's key is acrostic.triplet_nun_samekh_pe_partial: the review lane's finding is upheld, the cure author's rename is upheld on substance, and the orchestrator's block of the apply was correct because the scanner was enforcing the order as issued; the apply may now proceed under the narrowed predicate. CWO-1 stands as issued in the boss_lam_b1 ledger, which is not edited; from this ruling forward the deterministic scanner enforces CWO-1/B3-1, under which the bare tokens samekh and pe are Hebrew LETTER names permitted only inside the acrostic.* namespace and only without a mark-context co-token, while every mark-layer token (parashah, petuchah, setumah, mark) stays barred under every prefix and every compound the issued list named stays caught. The narrowing removes one token from the unconditional list (samekh) and, in the same act, closes a hole the issued list left open (a bare pe or samekh under a non-acrostic prefix, which can only be the mark, now fails). The price at the one site where the collision is live is an explicit never-conflated sentence in P02-006's device_notes.
rulings.grounds: 1. The conflict reproduces mechanically and is not a matter of reading: under CWO-1's issued token list the restored key is the sole hit over the 93 keys of the 26 rows (computed, in-memory substitution on rows_v5.jsonl); under the narrowed predicate the corpus returns 0 hits as filed and 0 hits with the key restored. 2. The letter name is the true name. The row's letters are a tier-1 byte fact: this poem's uniform triplets are byte-pinned in the toolkit's book facts and its pe-before-ayin order is pinned (B1-5 re-derived pe at position 16 on Lam.3.46-Lam.3.48 in the previous slice), so by the triplet arithmetic 3(k-1)+1..3k position 14 nun covers Lam.3.40-Lam.3.42, position 15 samekh Lam.3.43-Lam.3.45 and position 16 pe Lam.3.46-Lam.3.48; the span Lam.3.40-Lam.3.47 covers nun and samekh whole and enters pe. The positional key acrostic.triplet_pos16_partial_entry names only the partial pe entry and is silent on the two whole triplets the span carries, so it is not merely inconsistent but incomplete; the row's own boundary_rationale calls the letters the nun and samekh-letter triplets and the pe triplet, and 8 of the 9 F3 triplet keys are letter-named (the 17 rows of chs 1, 2 and 4 carry the generic acrostic.letter_boundary; only P02-006 carries a positional name - the brief's statement that every other acrostic key is letter-named is true of the F3 triplet keys, and that is the class that matters here). A positional formulation is also the class B1-5 ordered OUT of this very row's prose and the class CWO-6 bars in prose corpus-wide; a positional key reintroduces through the key what the orders removed from the prose. 3. What CWO-1 means for a letter token. The order's operative clause is its purpose: no key may name the parashah mark LAYER; the token list was the mechanism. The issued order itself already treats a bare letter name as permitted for pe - it bans only the compounds pe_mark, pe_close and poem_end_pe, which is why acrostic.triplet_pe_partial_ayin_tsade passes - and handled the book's other letter/mark homonym, samekh, asymmetrically by banning the bare token. Samekh is the only name in this witness that is at once a letter and a mark type with no compound to separate the two, so the asymmetry falls entirely on it. The hazard-catalog law added this session (a letter name is never a mark of the same name; the two layers are never conflated) cuts against the literal reading: suppressing the letter name because it is homonymous with the mark makes the tier-1 letter layer un-nameable in keys and is itself a conflation by suppression. The narrowing makes the order symmetric in the direction the order itself chose for pe. 4. Why narrow rather than uphold or merely clarify. Upholding would keep the corpus's only positional key, keep the key/prose mismatch, and enforce it by a scanner that treats a byte fact as a mark. Calling this a clarification would pretend the issued list did not say samekh; it did, the scanner enforced it correctly, and the campaign never rewrites history - so this is a NARROWING with its date and reason, the b1 ledger untouched, and every CWO-1 parity digit reported from here on names the predicate that produced it. 5. Why the tightening rides with the narrowing. The issued list let a bare pe pass under any non-acrostic prefix (closure.pe, hymn.pe) though nothing but the mark can be meant there; the namespace rule R2 closes that, and no filed key falls in it (0 hits as filed). CWO-9 stays the second guard: an acrostic.* key must have a letter object at a verse inside the span, so a mark disguised as a letter key fails there (chapter 5 carries no acrostic letter at all). 6. The predicate is mechanical, not judgement at each site: a tokenizer, three sets, three ordered rules, transliteration normalization to bar spelling-variant evasion, and 29 test vectors that the implementation must reproduce; the campaign's ngram7 tokenization of key sequences is unaffected by restoring one letter-named key. 7. The live collision site. Inside Lam.3.40-Lam.3.47 the samekh LETTER triplet (Lam.3.43-Lam.3.45) closes on a SAMEKH MARK at Lam.3.45 and a second SAMEKH mark stands at Lam.3.42; the span's front neighbour Lam.3.39 and its close-seam neighbour Lam.3.48 both carry SAMEKH, and the chapter's only PE mark stands at Lam.3.66 (all read from pmarks_Lam.json: 22 marked verses in this poem at every third verse). This is exactly the row where a reader could take the key's samekh for the mark, so the device_notes sentence that already pairs the lowercase letter names with the uppercase mark names must say the two are different layers.

consequence.revised_predicate_for_the_scanner: CWO-1 as narrowed by B3-1 (2026-09-07). Apply to every key of observed_substrate_signals in every row. STEP 1 tokenize: lower-case the key; prefix = the text before the first '.'; tokens = the key split on every '.' and '_' (empty pieces dropped); normalize transliteration variants before matching: samech, samek -> samekh; peh, fe, feh -> pe; parasha, parsha, parshah -> parashah; petucha, petuhah -> petuchah; setuma -> setumah. STEP 2 sets: MARK_ALWAYS = {parashah, parashot, parashiyot, petuchah, setumah, mark, marks, marked, marker, markers}; HOMONYM = {pe, samekh} (the two names that are at once a Hebrew letter and a mark type in this witness); MARK_CONTEXT = {close, closes, closed, closing, closure, end, ends, ending, poem, section, sections, break, division, open, opens, opening, layer, inventory, seg, segs, segment, type}. STEP 3 rules, in order: (R1) REJECT if tokens intersect MARK_ALWAYS - under ANY prefix, exactly as issued; (R2) REJECT if tokens intersect HOMONYM and prefix != 'acrostic' - a bare letter/mark homonym outside the acrostic namespace can only be the mark (this closes the hole in the issued list, under which e.g. closure.pe passed); (R3) REJECT if tokens intersect HOMONYM and tokens intersect MARK_CONTEXT - an acrostic key may not pair a letter name with mark wording (this keeps every compound the issued list named: pe_mark falls to R1, pe_close and poem_end_pe to R2 or R3 under every prefix); otherwise ACCEPT. The bare tokens pe and samekh are therefore letter names when and only when they stand under acrostic.* without a MARK_CONTEXT token; CWO-9 remains the second guard, since an acrostic.* key must have a letter object at a verse inside the span. TEST VECTORS (the implementation must reproduce all 29): ACCEPT acrostic.triplet_nun_samekh_pe_partial; acrostic.triplet_pe_partial_ayin_tsade; acrostic.letter_boundary; acrostic.triplet_alef_bet_gimel; closure.wrath_inclusio; closure.imprecatory_close; hymn.eternal_throne; acrostic.samekh_stanza; acrostic.pe_before_ayin_order; acrostic.triplet_pe_onset; closure.unresolved_close. REJECT closure.poem_end_pe; hymn.pe_close; divine_title.samekh; acrostic.pe_close; acrostic.samekh_mark; acrostic.triplet_samekh_setumah; closure.pe; acrostic.triplet_pe_partial_closing; acrostic.pe_section; parashah.pe; closure.samech_close; acrostic.triplet_samech_setuma; acrostic.peh_closed; voice.marks; closure.pe_mark; acrostic.samekh_layer; closure.PE_close; acrostic.triplet_pos16_partial_entry_mark. EXPECTED CORPUS DIGITS on rows_v5 (26 rows, 93 keys): 0 hits as filed; 0 hits with the P02-006 key restored; the issued list returns exactly 1 hit on the restored corpus (P02-006), which is the narrowed case. CWO-1's disclosure arm is unchanged: every mark disclosure lives in device_notes prose with the single-witness and tier-3-weak caveats and the never-conflated note. Reference implementation with these vectors: the boss's private scratch file lam_boss_b3_private/cwo1_b3_scan.py (private; the orchestrator re-implements it in the toolkit rather than importing it).

rulings.question: the reasoning record
rulings.grounds: 1. The gap is real and not curable from the orchestrator's side. The finding records attempts that ran to completion with a 0-byte transcript whose mtime never advanced past launch, a 40-cycle continuous snapshotter across a whole wave that added exactly one file, and a wave tally of 3 preserved transcripts of 11 tracked attempts (the escalation's later figure, 3 of 23 for the cycle, is the orchestrator's count and is not independently verifiable from the file I was given). The absent transcripts were never written; no capture cadence recovers a file that does not exist, and nothing exists for the books closed before this session. 2. Everything an agent DID and CLAIMED is already durable - deliverables, verbatim final messages with provenance, receipts, censuses, sweeps, apply and validator reports - so what is missing is only the record of how the agent reasoned: what it read, what it checked, what it reversed, what it doubted. A self-authored record captures precisely that class and nothing else the audit lacks. 3. Its known weakness is that it is self-authored and can be self-serving; the conditions below are designed around that weakness rather than pretending it away: the record is a CLAIM SET, never evidence; every entry must be of a form that can be checked against an artifact (a path, a verse ref, a tool run, a digit); quality adjectives are barred; zero doubts and any deviation are sampling triggers; and where the runtime does preserve a transcript the checker compares the record against it, so the record's fidelity is measured on a calibration set instead of assumed. 4. Cost is small and the change is additive and reversible: a bounded file of at most 800 words per attempt against attempts whose preserved transcripts run 0.9-1.5 MB; no shipped artifact changes; if the owner strikes it, the requirement lapses and the records already written stay as harmless durable files. The real cost is the audit obligation it creates, which is bounded by the schema and stated below. 5. Why the owner must see it, and why that does not pause the waves. OW-6 and OW-6c ask for an audit of chain of thought; the runtime does not reliably provide chain of thought; the record is a substitute for, not a fulfilment of, that clause, and only the owner can re-scope an owner directive or accept the coverage gap instead. That is a directive-interpretation question with campaign-wide blast radius, which is exactly the class OW-6 reserves for a human. But the decision is reversible, the cost of waiting is that further waves run with no reasoning artifact at all, and OW-5 pre-authorized proceeding book to book without a re-prompt - so the record is adopted now under delegated judgment, in force for the rest of the Lamentations cycle and for every following book until the owner rules, and the owner packet travels with the next owner touchpoint and no later than the Lamentations close packet. 6. The coverage statement is never replaced by the record: the OW-6 final check and the OW-6c packet list every attempt in one of three states - transcript and record, record only, neither - and say plainly that the pre-session books are in the third state.

what_it_must_contain: HEADER: attempt_id; lane/role; model as launched; effort as ORDERED and whether it was verified; the brief's exact path; the exact path(s) of the deliverable(s) the record describes. Schema name m8_reasoning_record.v1; fixed keys; JSON; at most 800 words in total.

INPUTS_READ: the exact path of every file the agent consumed, and every input the brief named that the agent did NOT read, declared as unread with the reason. Checkable against the tool-use receipt where one exists.

VERIFICATION_LEDGER: one entry per byte-level or digit claim the deliverable rests on - {claim, object (verse ref, key, field or file), tier, method (the toolkit tool and its arguments, or 'read from the pointed bytes'), result}. At least one entry per row or ruling the agent touched. No Hebrew bytes in the record (refs only; Hebrew is spliced only into deliverables, never re-typed into a record). This is the falsifiable core and the only reason the record is worth its cost.

REVERSALS: each conclusion the agent first reached and abandoned, the evidence that changed it, and where that evidence is (exact path or ref). An entry without an evidence reference is invalid and the checker treats it as a finding.
RESIDUAL_DOUBTS: each doubt with what would resolve it and its tier. An empty list is allowed only with the literal sentence 'no residual doubt' and is itself a sampling trigger for the checker.
DEVIATIONS_FROM_BRIEF: anything ordered that was not done, done differently, or a tool not run, with the reason; 'none' is allowed and is a claim the checker may test.

FORM RULES: written BEFORE the final message; the final message names the record's path (or states that it is embedded); the attempt receipt records the record's digest; quality adjectives (thorough, complete, verified, robust, exhaustive) are barred unless a ledger entry carries them; the record makes no claim the deliverable does not itself carry; the record is NEVER copied into row prose (the register purge E-06/E-18 binds) and is NEVER cited as evidence - it is a claim set reconciled against artifacts.

AUDIT OBLIGATION (this is the part that makes it worth having): the Fable final checker re-runs at least one deterministic ledger entry per record; re-derives the whole ledger for every record with zero doubts or any deviation; for every attempt whose transcript the runtime did preserve, compares the record against the transcript and reports fidelity (all such attempts while they are few, and never fewer than three per book once three exist) - that comparison calibrates trust in the record-only attempts; and lists every attempt in one of three states: transcript and record, record only, neither.
consequence.where_it_is_written: Default: a sibling file at the deliverable's exact path with the suffix .reasoning.json (for a JSONL deliverable, the same stem), the exact path named in the agent's brief under the E-19 exact-path law, mirrored to the durable store by the orchestrator's existing mirroring with its digest recorded in the attempt receipt. Only when a brief restricts the agent to one file, as this brief does, the record is embedded as a top-level reasoning_record object in that one deliverable. The first instance is embedded in this file.
consequence.cost_note: At most 800 words (roughly 1,200 output tokens) per attempt, well under one percent of an attempt whose preserved transcript runs 0.9-1.5 MB; brief text grows by one paragraph per lane. The recurring cost is the checker's per-record re-run and the calibration comparisons, bounded by the schema's size and the number of preserved transcripts. No shipped row, sweep, or report changes; adoption is reversible by striking one paragraph from the briefs.
consequence.effective: In force for every brief issued in the Lamentations cycle from this ruling forward and for every following book until the owner rules; not retroactive - attempts already complete are not re-run to produce one, and their state is reported as 'neither' or 'transcript only'.

owner_packet.question: The runtime does not reliably write subagent reasoning transcripts (3 of 11 attempts preserved at the wave tally; the orchestrator counts 3 of 23 for the cycle; the absent files were never written, a 40-cycle continuous snapshotter recovered one file, and nothing exists for the books closed before this session). Your OW-6 asks the final checker to audit 'everything written by a subagent even chain of thought', and OW-6c reserves an end-of-campaign re-check of 'all chain of thought'. Do you ratify the self-authored REASONING RECORD adopted here as the campaign's durable substitute, and re-scope OW-6 and OW-6c to: every durable subagent artifact (deliverables, verbatim final messages, receipts, reasoning records) plus every transcript the runtime happened to preserve, with per-attempt coverage stated in three states (transcript and record / record only / neither)? Or do you choose another course?
owner_packet.recommendation: Ratify the reasoning record with its conditions and re-scope OW-6/OW-6c as stated, with the explicit acknowledgement in the OW-6c packet that no chain of thought exists for the books closed before this session and that none can be recovered.
owner_packet.recommendation_reason: The capability you asked for is not available from the orchestrator's side and cannot be made available by any capture cadence; the record is cheap, additive and reversible; it is auditable wherever it makes a falsifiable claim, and its fidelity can be measured against the minority of transcripts the runtime does preserve; its limit - that it is self-authored - is disclosed and guarded rather than hidden. Doing nothing leaves roughly seven attempts in ten with no reasoning artifact of any kind.
owner_packet.decision_needed_by: Before the next book opens (the Lamentations close packet). Not blocking: the record is in force meanwhile under delegated judgment (OW-5, OW-6) and your correction is applied forward and recorded verbatim, append-only.

alternatives.choice: Ratify the reasoning record and re-scope OW-6/OW-6c (recommended)
pros: cheap (under one percent of an attempt) and reversible
auditable against artifacts; fidelity measured on the transcripts that do exist
cons: self-authored, so not raw reasoning and open to self-serving framing
creates a real audit obligation for the final checker
could be mistaken for chain-of-thought coverage if a packet is careless about the three states

alternatives.choice: Reject the record and accept the gap: the OW-6 audit covers deliverables, final messages and receipts only
pros: no added output or audit work
no risk of a false sense of coverage
cons: the chain-of-thought requirement goes unmet for most attempts with no mitigation
nothing records what an agent read, reversed or doubted
the OW-6c end-of-campaign re-check has nothing new to read

alternatives.choice: Fix capture at the runtime or harness level (owner-side: launch mode, an SDK transcript hook, or a wrapper that persists every agent message)
pros: the only path to raw, non-self-authored reasoning
would also cover the transcripts the runtime currently drops
cons: outside the orchestrator's and the boss's authority; feasibility unknown
may pause waves while it is built and tested
still nothing for the books already closed

alternatives.choice: Require the record only from decision-bearing lanes (boss, checkers, reviewers, cure authors) and not from writer or sweep lanes
cons: writer and sweep lanes originate most byte claims and most reversals
partial coverage that the OW-6c packet would have to explain
